design.purpose: finally doing the tax return (traits: novelty_seeking: moderate; sustained_attention_on_boring_tasks: weak)

text: So the tax return is done. Submitted, receipt number and everything (I screenshotted it twice, because I trust nothing). The deadline is end of January and I filed on the 9th, so no panic fees this year. First job was getting the invoices into one folder, and that was easy because Hollis, my biggest client, pays by bank transfer and every payment has a reference (bless them). The software receipts took ages. There are eleven subscriptions, I counted, and two I had forgotten I even had. Around the third evening I caught myself comparing invoicing apps instead of typing in figures, and I bought a year of one, which is not a deduction I planned for. My dad died in April and I've been low on and off since, so some evenings I just sat there with the spreadsheet open and did very little. What worked was forty minutes after lunch with the radio off and a timer on my phone, anything longer and I was reorganising my desktop folders. My accountant friend checked the totals and found one wrong VAT figure, the supplier's typo, not mine. Refund should land in about three weeks (fingers crossed, the boiler needs a service).
